newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI suspends domestic bourse.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI suspends domestic bourse.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) chief said on Friday it had suspended the governing board of a domestic bourse for six months due to "irregularities".

D.R. Mehta said SEBI has appointed W.S. Tambe, a former director on the board of India's central bank, as the administrator of the Pune Stock Exchange, one of 23 bourses across India, with immediate effect.
This was the first time a stock exchange board is being superseded in India, Mehta said.
The exchange was superseded due to irregularities involving its five board members, he told reporters.
Mehta said SEBI had already served notices on 25 brokers at the exchange suspending their licences while investigation was under way against 15 other brokers.
"These brokers including many governing body members were involved in illegal "badla" (carry-forward trade), evasion of margins and not reporting their trade to the exchange," he said.
